subject: Accelerated commitment step-down — pricing approval request
messages:
From: Macy Thompson <macy@orionhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal v3 — ask on step-down pricing and onboarding credit

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the fast turnaround on the draft. A few items from the exec team: we can commit to the stated 12-month minimum at the Level-2 throughput for year 1, but we need a softened rate in years 2–3 (an intentional step-down tied to expected usage drop post-rollout).

Specifically: would Redwood consider a 45% list discount in year 1 with an automatic step-down to 25% in year 2 and 15% in year 3, combined with a $150k onboarding credit to offset integration work? Our legal ops also asked for a clause that locks the step-down schedule in the SOW.

We attached our internal SOW amendments for context (see proposal v3). Goal is to close the commercial terms this month.

Best,
Macy
Macy Thompson
Head of Platform Partnerships
OrionHealth Systems

Attachments: orion_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal PDF, 12 pages)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal v3 — ask on step-down pricing and onboarding credit

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Orion's request. Key asks: 45% year-1, 25% year-2, 15% year-3 plus $150k onboarding credit and an SOW clause for automatic step-down.

Quick summary of why this matters: Orion is a high-profile health vertical reference and a likely channel for a marketplace placement. They bring estimated token volumes that should meet our dedicated capacity thresholds in year 1 but risk falling under our Tier-2 economics in year 2 if usage drops. The revenue impact of the requested schedule versus our standard ramp is roughly a 22% reduction in ARR across the contract term vs our baseline.

Suggested internal options:
- Option A (preferred sales): Approve a front-loaded concession: 40% Y1, 25% Y2, 15% Y3 + $100k onboarding credit, with forfeiture of credit if onboarding milestones not met.
- Option B (finance-friendly): Standard list discount of 30% Y1 with a structured rebate that pays back if usage targets fall below threshold (protects us vs churn).

We need VP/CFO-level approval to deviate from our standard discount guardrails. Can you review and advise whether we can sign off on Option A (sales ask) or push Option B? If approved, we'll hand to Legal for the SOW clause and DocuSign.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal v3 — ask on step-down pricing and onboarding credit

Jonas — I ran a quick model and attached a compact comparison (pricing-comparison.xlsx). My read: Option A gets the deal closed faster but increases revenue risk; Option B preserves our unit economics but will slow acceptance (rebate admin overhead).

I'm inclined to recommend a hybrid: 40% Y1, 25% Y2, 15% Y3 + $100k onboarding credit, conditional on two milestones: (1) integration sign-off within 90 days, (2) adoption milestone of X active pipelines by month 6 — failure to meet both triggers an automatic step-up reconciliation (we bill a backcharge to recover 50% of credit). That gives us recovery levers while keeping the commercial story simple for the customer.

As this exceeds our standard concession limit for VP signoff, @Marissa — can you confirm if you (VP/CFO) can greenlight the hybrid structure? If yes, I will prepare the commercial memo for Legal and Finance to include the milestone language and DocuSign packet.

Attachments: pricing-comparison.xlsx (summary table)

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal v3 — ask on step-down pricing and onboarding credit (VP/CFO approval)

Thanks team — I reviewed Ben's model and the attachments. I approve the hybrid concession as outlined: 40% Y1, 25% Y2, 15% Y3 with a $100k onboarding credit, subject to the two milestones Ben specified (integration sign-off within 90 days; adoption milestone by month 6). Recovery clause to reconcile 50% of the credit if both milestones are missed.

Notes for Legal/Finance:
- Please add explicit milestone definitions and the backcharge mechanics to the SOW so it's self-executing.
- Cap the concession exposure to $1.2M over the contract term (this is the maximum acceptable revenue delta).
- DocuSign packet should include: commercial SOW (with step-down table), milestone matrix, and a 30-day termination for convenience with pro-rated refund mechanics.

Jonas — you have VP/CFO signoff; proceed to Legal to finalize language and generate DocuSign. Ben — loop in Finance for the billing reconciliation template. Marcus — please ensure the dedicated capacity booking is tentatively reserved for Q3 pending signature.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations (acting CFO approval)
Redwood Inference
